Last Friday (the 21st), during the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing into a police vehicle during the early morning hours. In response to inquiries, police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

Shortly after 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer claimed that a shirt worn by a woman in the queue was "suspected of carrying some seditious intent" and escorted her away in a police vehicle. While officers were taking the woman away, several officers directed reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and stretched orange cordon tape toward YIng Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they packed up the cordon tape. A "court-watching companion" queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) inquired with police about the reason the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. Police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and is currently being detained for investigation.
